newsitem.title: USA: Calif. groups allege improper gift for tax measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. groups allege improper gift for tax measure.

text.p: Taxpayer groups on Tuesday accused the League of California Cities of making an allegedly improper $50,000 contribution to try to defeat a controversial tax initiative on the November state ballot.

"It (the contribution) is not only outrageous but it is likely illegal," said attorney Jonathan Coupal, director of legal affairs for the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, a chief sponsor of Proposition 218.
If approved by California voters in November, Proposition 218 would limit the ability of local governments to impose taxes, fees and assessments.
Coupal and several other taxpayer groups made the allegation at a news conference in Sacramento.
Don Benninghoven, executive director of the League of California Cities, countered that the $50,000 donation came from private funds not tax funds.
"The private funds come from processing fees for federally-authorized bonds for California business expansion, job expansion and low-cost housing," Benninghoven said.
The League is a $4 million a year lobbying and educational representative of some 400 California cities.
Coupal said the funds should be returned to the cities.
